questions.question: What does a steady green traffic light mean?

options.text: You can go through the intersection at a safe speed if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can go through the intersection at a safe speed if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A steady green light means you may proceed through the intersection. First, make sure the intersection is clear of other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: Children do not react as quickly as adults.
Children are smaller and harder to see.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, playgrounds, and parks. They may ride onto the road without warning.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction zones?
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers of a school zone. It alerts you that children or pedestrians may be crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you an intersection is coming up so you can prepare to turn or watch for traffic.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross in the middle of the street outside a crosswalk, what should you do?

options.text: You do not have to stop for them.

questions.explanation: You must stop for pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally or not in a crosswalk.

questions.question: Which of these is illegal?

options.text: Passing another vehicle in a no passing zone.
Passing another vehicle over a railroad crossing.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass when there is a solid yellow line next to your lane, in no passing zones, at street crossings, or at railroad crossings. Do not pass when the car ahead has stopped for a pedestrian or in work zones where it is unsafe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop suddenly.
questions.explanation: Slow down when entering a work zone. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and hazards.

questions.question: Why is night driving more difficult?

options.text: Speed limits are higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you can only see as far as your headlights shine. This makes it difficult to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are going.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns you that a side road will cross ahead. Stay alert.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, what must you do?

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks. You must stop for pedestrians, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: Which of these causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching the road and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Speeding is a common cause of crashes. Always drive at the speed limit and adjust your speed for road conditions.

questions.question: If someone is injured in an accident, when must you report it?
questions.explanation: You must call the police right away if anyone is injured. Leaving the scene before police arrive is a crime.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: What is the best way to change lanes?

options.text: When a car is in your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully, only when needed. Each lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both parts of a two-part seat belt. Using only one part gives you less protection. Even with an automatic shoulder belt, always buckle the lap belt too.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop. Come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction of the arrow. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.

questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a right turn at this intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic signals are coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: When approaching a person crossing the street with a white cane or guide dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.
Honk your horn as you proceed past them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.
questions.explanation: When you see a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop. Wait until the person is completely clear of your path. Always give blind pedestrians the right-of-way.

questions.question: Which statement is true about changing lanes?

options.text: You only need to turn and look over your right shoulder for lane changes to the right or left.
Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
Vehicles with two outside mirrors do not have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and your left shoulder for a left lane change.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal and check your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. For a right lane change, look over your right shoulder. For a left lane change, look over your left shoulder. This ensures no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in the next lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Bicycles do not have turn signals. Bicyclists use hand and arm signals instead. When a bicyclist extends their left arm straight out, they are signaling a left turn.

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.

questions.explanation: Keep a three- to four-second following distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Riding too close endangers both of you. If the motorcyclist falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting them. The risk of falling is higher on wet roads, icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and you see a pedestrian crossing your lane, you should:

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are crossing your lane. This is true even if there is no marked crosswalk.

questions.question: When driving in fog, it is best to drive with:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off the moisture in the air and make visibility worse.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed. You may see this sign at intersections where oncoming traffic is heavy.

questions.question: "No passing zone" signs tell drivers:

options.text: That it is not safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: That it is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass another vehicle in that area. These signs are placed where visibility is poor and passing would be unsafe.

questions.question: You are required to stop your vehicle:

options.text: At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.
Where there is a red traffic light.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a red traffic light. You must also obey any stop order from a police officer directing traffic, regardless of what the signs or signals say.
